text:
samir: heads-up — opened a tiny PR to add a lint step and a couple of example fixes for schema-anchored function responses. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412

jessica: nice, can you summarize the actual rule the linter enforces? i skimmed but want to make sure it won't break livedocs consumers

samir: sure — rule is `response-schema-no-ambiguous-null` — it flags union types like `string | null` inside tool outputs and requires an explicit wrapper object or `nullable: true` in the example so parsers don't guess. the goal is reliable parsing for SDKs and snippets.

liam: sounds good. will this change affect the `tool-caller` examples in the JS SDK?

samir: yes, a few examples needed small edits — updated `js/snippets/` and `python/snippets/` in the PR. sample change: `{"result": null}` -> `{"result": {"value": null, "present": false}}` (we include a tiny presence field)

priya: quick ask — we should keep a migration note in /docs/migration/function-calling.md. otherwise users upgrading might be confused by parser behaviour. i can draft a short blurb.

morgan: ran the lint job locally — caught two more edge cases: array-of-nullable unions like `string[] | null` inside a tool output. i pushed a tiny test to the PR that demonstrates the failing parse.

samir: thanks! added a follow-up commit to handle arrays by normalizing to `items` objects and explicit `nullable` flags in the snippet generator.

docs-bot: build failed on `docs-site` — broken link detected: /docs/old-toolcall-guide -> 404 (CI job: docs-link-check)

jessica: ahhh that old guide was renamed last quarter. samir can you add a redirect or update the link in the migration doc?

samir: will do. planning to: 1) add migration note, 2) update all snippets in JS + Python, 3) add CI unit tests that assert example output parses with the SDKs. timeline: today if no blockers.

liam: i can review JS snippets — will check for edgecases in `function-calling` client helper. prioritize any examples used in Quickstart.

priya: i'll take the migration doc wording, keep it short: explain why we disallow ambiguous nulls, show a 2-line snippet before/after, link to SDK compatibility table.

morgan: FYI i replaced two deprecated links in `snippets/` and added tests in `tools/snippet-validator` to run sample outputs through `python` and `node` parsers. committing shortly.

jessica: once tests pass, can we add a note to the release PR (v1.9.0) about doc breaking changes? product wants a heads-up email to customers using `function-calling` in prod.

samir: yes — I'll add a short entry under "Docs/Breaking changes" and ping eng-sales for a quick buyer-facing blurb.

morgan: PR is green locally. opening a tiny follow-up to fix the link-check CI error and the redirect.

samir: thanks everyone. next steps: liam review JS snippets, priya write migration blurb, morgan push CI fix, jessica add release note. i'll merge after green CI and two approvals. :thumbsup:

liam: on it, aiming to review in the next hour.

priya: drafted migration paragraph and pushed to `priya/migration-note` branch — putting the before/after JSON inline so copy-paste is easy.

jessica: awesome. ping me when the PR updates and i'll add the release blurb.

samir: merging now once the redirect diff lands. thanks team!

morgan: redirect diff up — CI re-run queued.

docs-bot: CI passed — all checks green. merge allowed.

samir: merged. tagging `#docs-release` channel and adding a short changelog entry.

jessica: nice work, low-friction migration for users and cleaner examples for SDKs.

priya: can we add a short note in the Quickstart to prefer presence-wrapper patterns? a single line recommendation might avoid future breakage.

samir: good call — adding that to the Quickstart patch in a follow-up.

morgan: leaving a comment on the release PR with links to the updated examples across languages.

samir: done. closing thread. :rocket:
